frames.observation: The authored hooked beak, crown, chest, paired wings, legs, talons, and tail form one readable Roc silhouette in settled idle.
The native airborne attack pose keeps the torso, wing roots, broad feathers, legs, and tail connected; the top of the head is cropped by the combat camera in this frame.
The ordinary hit is visible as a 10-point health change at the transition into damageLight_roc. Impact effects partly cover the chest, while both wings and the body remain continuous.
The later native critical attack pose keeps the beak, torso, wings, legs, talons, and tail attached while effects and combat UI obscure some surfaces.
The explicit fixture shows the authored Roc folded and lowered under deathHeavy_roc with both wings and the tail still visibly connected. This is animated death, not a body ragdoll.
The native row portrait is readable at 328 by 280 and clearly shows the authored beak, eye, crown, head, and neck mantle.

conclusion: The reviewed exact-source originals show a coherent authored Roc through idle, native attacks, ordinary hit response, animated fixture death, and the constructed native row portrait.
limits: Six selected originals were reviewed rather than every rendered pose or camera angle.
Combat UI, the hero, hit flashes, depth effects, and the victory state obscure some surfaces.
The explicit KillSingle fixture is not ordinary lethal-damage evidence.
m_DoRagdoll is false across all retained combat capture frames, so the recorded death is animated rather than a body ragdoll.
The retained frames do not establish a settled corpse, precise visible corpse lifetime, final resource disposal, full culling coverage, or finished art direction.
The portrait evidence is one constructed native row caller at one resolution. It is not an opened encounter menu or live combat HUD.
This review covers only rocA and enRoc01 renderer 121238. It does not establish rocB, rocJungleA, or another bird rig.
